panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A shows Hematoxylin and Eosin stained tissue of a mitral valve from a patient with Maroteaux-Lamy syndrome, demonstrating stromal infiltration and clear cells. B: Panel B shows Alcian Blue 2,5 staining of the mitral valve, confirming glycosaminoglycan storage associated with MPS VI. C: Panel C shows immunohistochemical staining for CD68 in the mitral valve, identifying clear cells as macrophages, a feature of chronic inflammation/pathology in MPS VI. D: Panel D shows immunohistochemical staining for Actin in the mitral valve, highlighting myofibroblasts and clear cells, consistent with the histopathology described in MPS VI.

She had peripheral corneal clouding, causing visual blurring. Other notable deformities noted were kyphoscoliosis, pectus excavatum, and radial, humeral, and ulnar deformities restricting the range of motion. Cardiac auscultation was notable for normal heart sounds and a Grade III/VI systolic murmur at the second right intercostal space and long mid-diastolic murmur at the apex.

The electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm, normal QRS axis, and left atrial enlargement. The chest radiogram showed a typical ‘double density’ left atrial shadow, straightening of the left heart border, and dilated main pulmonary artery (Figure 1B).
